_foreignNote: Sites on a country domain outside the U.S. (.ca, .ch, .uz, .co.uk, .com.au, and every other two-letter country ending except .us and the U.S. territories .gu .as .mp .vi .pr .um) are never shown, and a source on one is not fetched. List a site in allowHosts to let it through, and in gatedHosts to let through only some of its stories.
_gateNote: A site in allowHosts can also be listed here to let through only some of its stories: a story from it (matched by its address, the address Google News reports for its publisher, or its name) is kept when its headline and summary match require (or, with community: true, name the communities in communityPattern) and do not match deny. rnz.co.nz: Pacific Islander stories only, no sports. independent.co.uk: stories about Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander communities only.

_pacificNote: Pacific island nations. A story about a Pacific island country (Fiji's constitution, a Samoan prime minister, a drug-detection unit in Tonga) is not about Pacific Islander communities in the United States, so a news story that names one of the pacificNations without a tie to the U.S. is dropped from every source. A tie is any usTie word (matched ignoring case) or usTieCase word (matched exactly, so "US" and "ICE" do not match the words "us" and "ice"): the U.S. and its government and military, the Compact of Free Association, nuclear testing, climate change, and the U.S. territories and states. A gated site with "tie": true (rnz.co.nz) needs a tie for every story. Statements, policy items, research and the community outlets are not checked, and a story the owner pinned or featured stays. Add a word to usTie to keep more stories; remove pacificNations to turn the rule off.

A news story that uses a Pacific place only as a destination (a TV star's exhausting trip to Guam, a K-pop idol's honeymoon in Hawaii) is dropped when it names one of the travelPlaces together with one of the travelWords and does not name the communities (communityPattern).
